title: TypeScript SDK: stable type fingerprints, streaming-friendly discriminators, and Zod/JSON Schema glue
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Problem: Consumers of the TypeScript SDK rely on generated type identifiers and discriminator patterns to validate structured model output. Currently we see: drift in generated type IDs between runs, brittle runtime discriminators for streaming responses, and duplicated Zod/JSON Schema helpers that diverge from codegen. Goal: produce stable, content-aware type fingerprints, adapt discriminated-union detection to streaming partial events, and consolidate Zod/JSON Schema helper generation into a single, testable pipeline that is compatible with progressive parsing and retry semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Generated type fingerprints remain stable across identical model schema inputs (fingerprint algorithm and seed documented)
Runtime discriminator helpers can resolve union shape from streaming token batches where discriminator tag may arrive mid-stream
tsdk exposes a single helper module that emits Zod validators and JSON Schema artifacts from the canonical model descriptors
Migration guide for downstream SDK consumers and internal SDK examples updated
End-to-end tests cover streaming parse + retry + fallback to permissive validator
Performance: fingerprint and helper generation adds < 150ms to CLI codegen run on CI macOS agent
tasks: Design fingerprint format and collision properties (RFC)
Implement deterministic fingerprinting in codegen (TypeScript emitter)
Extend streaming parser to buffer until discriminator tag appears and then apply shape validator incrementally
Create Zod/JSON Schema generator that reuses codegen AST nodes and emits both artifacts from same source
Add retry-aware validation policy (strict on first pass, permissive on retry/fallback)
Write unit and integration tests for progressive parse scenarios (simulated partial chunks)
Add examples in docs repo and sample app showing migration steps
Create rollout plan and feature flag for new validators
